Reality Distortion Field

A phrase associated with Steve Jobs for persuasive confidence that can reshape how other people judge what is possible.

  • People
  • Technology
  • Vocabulary

Context

Often abbreviated RDF, the phrase was used by Bud Tribble to describe Steve Jobs in 1981, as recounted by Macintosh team member Andy Hertzfeld. The description combines charisma, insistence, and the ability to make an ambitious outcome feel achievable.

The phrase is often used when discussing the boundary between motivating people to exceed expectations and persuading them to discount practical limits.

Examples

  • A team initially calls a deadline impossible, then leaves a presentation convinced that the project can be finished in time.

References

  • Andy Hertzfeld’s account at Folklore.org
